hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker crashes on one specific message, msg-453808 at offset 495220, with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at expandReferences'. This points to a self-referencing or deeply recursive payload. Each restart picks up again at the same committed offset (#240, #246, #264) and crashes on the same message, which is what keeps the pod in CrashLoopBackOff while lag on notifications.outbound grows. The crash keeps happening after the pods are back on v3.4.1 (#239 onward), so the message is the problem, not the code. The other services logged no errors.

v4.20.8 rolled out about 70 seconds before the first crash. But the restarted pods run v3.4.1 and fail the same way on the same message, so the deploy probably isn't the cause, though it could have produced the bad message.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip msg-453808 (offset 495220) or move it to a dead-letter queue by committing past it, so the worker can resume and work through the lag. Then fix expandReferences so it detects reference cycles and has a depth limit, and wrap per-message processing in error handling that sends bad messages to the DLQ instead of crashing the process. Check the producer to see how a self-referencing payload got published.
